claim: The input side of RL top-8 pairs is fixed by base activations and the output side by the reward, so Think-SFT sits in Math 3.1 top-8 subspace much less on the output side than the input side, relative to Math 3.0 (Q in [0.05, 0.7]).

On-policy RL shares the output side of the deliberation pairs whatever the reward while Think-SFT overlaps only the driven inputs, so relative to its input-side capture Code-RL 3.1 sits on Math 3.1 top-8 output side far more than Think-SFT (Q_C in [1.4, 8.0]).
Code's pairs at 1x shift every sample by a graded amount, so on cued-solved problems m21's deliberative and non-deliberative answers differ little, G in [-0.10, 0.17].
Under S3 the edit and RL only lower the chance-slip rate, so N(E,R) equals N(B,R) and D lies in [-0.10, 0.07].
